    Learning¶

    eden.learning holds learning-side code that is not a task: policy export, and algorithms that extend an RL library. A task selects an algorithm in its runner_options through an options class whose class_name names the implementation, so eden train --task <name> trains it and a saved config.json resumes through it. The training runs guide explains runners and custom algorithms; the runner options themselves are on the learning options page.

    Policy export¶

    eden export writes policy.onnx, policy.pt (TorchScript) and policy_spec.json for a runtime outside Eden. See the policy export guide.

    Export a trained policy for a runtime outside Eden: an ONNX / TorchScript graph plus policy_spec.json.

    eden export (:func:eden.utils.cli.tasks.export_task) builds the checkpoint's own env, loads the runner, and hands both to :func:export_policy, which writes

    • policy.onnx — input obs (the actor's observation groups, concatenated, un-normalized), output actions (the raw policy output, before the action terms scale it), with a dynamic batch axis. A recurrent policy also takes h_in (and c_in for an LSTM), shaped (num_layers, batch, hidden), and returns h_out (c_out): the caller threads the state, starting from zeros;
    • policy.pt — the same composition as TorchScript, batch 1 when recurrent: its hidden state lives in the module, and reset() zeroes it;
    • policy_spec.json — the contract around the graph (:func:build_policy_spec): what fills obs, how actions becomes joint targets, the control rate, and where the graph came from.

    The observation normalizer is part of both graphs. The graph comes from the policy model's own as_onnx() / as_jit() (rsl-rl-lib >= 4's export hooks), which is also how a learner overrides the default: RMA's :class:~eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl.rma.model.RmaActorModel defines both to export its deployment composition (estimator injected). An inherited hook can export something other than what the model runs, so every export is checked against the runner's inference policy on the env's own observations before anything is written (:func:verify_export). The files are written into a staging directory and moved into place only once checked, so a failed export leaves the output directory as it was.

    The spec records the robot's nominal command: the joint-zero offset domain randomization draws per env is left out of the action offset, and an env whose default pose itself was randomized at startup is refused (:func:disable_contract_randomization strips those terms from a config before it is built).

    def export_policy(
    runner: Any,
    env: RslRlVecEnvWrapper,
    out_dir: str,
    *,
    formats: tuple[str, ...] = EXPORT_FORMATS,
    task: str,
    checkpoint: str,
    verify: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Export ``runner``'s policy to ``out_dir`` and write ``policy_spec.json`` beside it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runner:
        An rsl_rl runner with ``checkpoint`` loaded.
    env:
        The env the runner was built on: the observations the export is checked on, and what the spec describes.
    out_dir:
        Directory to write into (created if missing). An earlier export there is replaced, and a graph of a format
        not exported this time is removed with it; on a failure the directory is left as it was.
    formats:
        Any of :data:`EXPORT_FORMATS`.
    task:
        The registered task name, recorded in the spec.
    checkpoint:
        The checkpoint path, hashed into the spec.
    verify:
        Check every exported graph against the runner's inference policy (:func:`verify_export`) before writing the
        spec. The ONNX check needs ``onnxruntime``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, str]
        ``{format: path}`` for every file written, the spec under ``"spec"``.
    """
    unknown = sorted(set(formats) - set(EXPORT_FORMATS))
    if unknown or not formats:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Export formats {unknown or list(formats)} are not supported; choose one or more of {EXPORT_FORMATS}."
        )
    check_export_dependencies(formats, verify=verify)
    get_policy = getattr(getattr(runner, "alg", None), "get_policy", None)
    if get_policy is None:
        raise TypeError(
            f"{type(runner).__qualname__} has no `alg.get_policy()`, so there is no policy model to export. Export "
            f"reads the model through it, as rsl-rl-lib >= 4's algorithms provide it; under rsl-rl-lib 3, upgrade "
            f"(a 3.x checkpoint loads into a 4.x / 5.x runner)."
        )
    policy = get_policy()
    obs_groups = policy_obs_groups(policy)
    refuse_randomized_contract(env.unwrapped)
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    # Staged, then moved in only once checked and described: a graph that failed its check, or a spec cut short, must
    # not land where a deployment could pick it up, nor beside the files of an earlier export.
    staging = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".eden-export-", dir=out_dir)
    try:
        staged = {}
        for fmt in EXPORT_FORMATS:
            if fmt in formats:
                staged[fmt] = os.path.join(staging, EXPORT_FILENAMES[fmt])
                (_export_onnx if fmt == "onnx" else _export_jit)(policy, staged[fmt])
        if verify:
            verify_export(staged, runner.get_inference_policy(device=env.device), env, obs_groups)
        spec = build_policy_spec(env.unwrapped, policy, staged, task=task, checkpoint=checkpoint, runner_env=env)
        staged["spec"] = os.path.join(staging, POLICY_SPEC_FILENAME)
        with open(staged["spec"], "w") as f:
            json.dump(spec, f, indent=2)
            f.write("\n")
        files = {key: os.path.join(out_dir, os.path.basename(path)) for key, path in staged.items()}
        for key, path in staged.items():  # the spec last, so it never names a graph not yet in place
            os.replace(path, files[key])
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
    for fmt in EXPORT_FORMATS:
        stale = os.path.join(out_dir, EXPORT_FILENAMES[fmt])
        if fmt not in files and os.path.exists(stale):
            os.remove(stale)  # an earlier export's graph, which the new spec does not describe
    return files

    def check_export_dependencies(formats: tuple[str, ...], *, verify: bool) -> None:
    """Raise ``ImportError`` if a package ``formats`` needs is missing: ``onnx`` for the ONNX graph's spec, and
    ``onnxruntime`` to check it.

    ``eden export`` calls this before it builds anything, so a missing extra costs no env build.
    """
    if "onnx" not in formats:
        return
    missing = []
    for package in ("onnx", "onnxruntime") if verify else ("onnx",):
        try:
            importlib.import_module(package)
        except (ImportError, OSError) as exc:  # a broken onnxruntime-gpu wheel fails on its CUDA libraries
            missing.append(f"{package} ({' '.join(str(exc).split())})")
    if missing:
        skip = " onnxruntime only runs the parity check, which --no_verify (verify=False) skips." if verify else ""
        raise ImportError(
            f"Exporting the ONNX graph needs {' and '.join(missing)}. Install the extra with {install_hint('onnx')} "
            f"(for the GPU wheel: {install_hint('onnx-gpu')}). Or export TorchScript only with --format jit.{skip}"
        )

    def disable_contract_randomization(config: EdenRLConfig) -> list[str]:
    """Disable ``config``'s event terms that would randomize what the spec records as nominal; return their names.

    Call it before the env is built: ``eden export`` does. :func:`export_policy` refuses an env built with them.
    """
    from eden.managers.event_manager import EVENT_TERM_REGISTRY

    if config.event_options is None:
        return []
    disabled = []
    for name in config.event_options.term_keys():
        term_cls = EVENT_TERM_REGISTRY.get(getattr(config.event_options, name).name)
        if isinstance(term_cls, type) and issubclass(term_cls, _contract_randomization_terms()):
            config.event_options.disable_term(name)
            disabled.append(name)
    return disabled

    def refuse_randomized_contract(env: RLEnvBase) -> None:
    """Raise ``ValueError`` if ``env`` was built with an event term that randomizes what the spec records as nominal."""
    event_manager = getattr(env, "event_manager", None)
    if event_manager is None:
        return
    randomizing = {
        name: type(term).__name__
        for _, name, term in event_manager.iter_terms()
        if isinstance(term, _contract_randomization_terms())
    }
    if randomizing:
        listed = ", ".join(f"'{name}' ({cls})" for name, cls in randomizing.items())
        raise ValueError(
            f"The env was built with event term(s) {listed}, which bias each env's default joint pose at startup, so "
            f"policy_spec.json would record env 0's random draw as the robot's default pose and action offset. Build "
            f"the env from a config passed through eden.learning.export.disable_contract_randomization(config) "
            f"first, as eden export does; reading another env's row would only record another draw."
        )

    def policy_obs_groups(policy: Any) -> list[str]:
    """The observation groups ``policy`` concatenates into its input, in order — the layout of the graph's ``obs``."""
    groups = getattr(policy, "obs_groups", None)
    if not isinstance(groups, (list, tuple)) or not groups:
        raise TypeError(
            f"{type(policy).__qualname__} has no `obs_groups` list, so the observation layout of an export cannot be "
            f"known. Export reads the groups the model concatenates from that attribute, as rsl-rl-lib >= 4's "
            f"MLPModel sets it; a custom model must set it too."
        )
    return list(groups)

    def verify_export(files: dict[str, str], inference_policy: Any, env: RslRlVecEnvWrapper, obs_groups: list[str]) -> None:
    """Check every exported graph reproduces ``inference_policy`` over :data:`VERIFY_STEPS` real control steps.

    The env is stepped by ``inference_policy`` from its current state, under ``torch.inference_mode`` as rsl_rl's
    rollout steps it; each graph then replays the same observations from a zero recurrent state.
    ``inference_policy`` is what ``eden inference`` runs, so a learner whose export hook exports anything else — an
    inherited ``as_onnx()`` that skips the model's own forward — fails here, before a spec is written next to it.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        Naming the format, the step and the largest deviation, when a graph disagrees.
    """
    reset = getattr(inference_policy, "reset", None)
    if reset is not None:
        reset()
    observations, expected = [], []
    obs = env.get_observations()
    # inference_mode, as rsl_rl's own rollout steps the env: after a `learn()` its buffers are inference tensors,
    # which only an inference-mode step may update in place.
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for _ in range(VERIFY_STEPS):
            actions = inference_policy(obs)
            observations.append(torch.cat([obs[group] for group in obs_groups], dim=-1).cpu())
            expected.append(actions.cpu())
            obs, *_ = env.step(actions)
    for fmt, path in files.items():
        produced = _run_onnx(path, observations) if fmt == "onnx" else _run_jit(path, observations)
        name = os.path.basename(path)
        for step, (got, want) in enumerate(zip(produced, expected, strict=True)):
            if got.shape != want.shape:
                mismatch = f"actions of shape {tuple(got.shape)} where the policy returned {tuple(want.shape)}"
            elif not torch.allclose(got, want, atol=VERIFY_ATOL, rtol=VERIFY_RTOL):
                mismatch = (
                    f"actions up to {(got - want).abs().max().item():.3e} away from the policy's "
                    f"(tolerance atol={VERIFY_ATOL}, rtol={VERIFY_RTOL})"
                )
            else:
                continue
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"The exported {fmt} graph ({name}) does not reproduce the policy: at step {step} it returned {mismatch}. "
                f"The model's export hook exports something other than what it runs; fix the hook rather than the "
                f"tolerance."
            )

    def build_policy_spec(
    env: RLEnvBase,
    policy: Any,
    files: dict[str, str],
    *,
    task: str,
    checkpoint: str,
    runner_env: RslRlVecEnvWrapper | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The ``policy_spec.json`` contract for ``policy`` as built on ``env``.

    Sections: ``model`` (the files and their tensors), ``observations`` (what fills ``obs``, slice by slice),
    ``actions`` (how ``actions`` becomes a command), ``entities`` (each commanded entity's DOFs in column order,
    with default positions and PD gains), ``rate`` and ``provenance``. ``runner_env`` is the rsl_rl wrapper, for
    its action clip. ``env`` must pass :func:`refuse_randomized_contract`, as :func:`export_policy` checks first.
    """
    obs_groups = policy_obs_groups(policy)
    clip_actions = getattr(runner_env, "clip_actions", None)
    action_terms = _action_spec(env)
    return {
        "schema_version": POLICY_SPEC_SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "model": _model_spec(files),
        "observations": _observation_spec(env, obs_groups),
        "actions": {
            "dim": env.action_manager.total_action_dim,
            "clip": None if clip_actions is None else [-float(clip_actions), float(clip_actions)],
            "terms": action_terms,
        },
        "entities": _entity_spec(env, {term["entity_name"] for term in action_terms if term.get("dofs_name")}),
        "rate": {
            "control_dt": float(env.dt),
            "decimation": int(env.env_options.decimation),
            "sim_dt": float(env.env_options.sim_dt),
        },
        "provenance": _provenance(env, task, checkpoint),
    }

    rsl-rl-lib algorithms¶

    eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl holds one subpackage per algorithm. Each has an options module (what a task configures) next to the implementation.

    Models, algorithms and runners for rsl-rl-lib 5, selected through their options' class_name.

    • :mod:.simba — a SimBaV2 actor / critic behind one encoder per observation group.
    • :mod:.muon_ppo — PPO whose optimizer is Muon for the 2-D weights and AdamW for the rest.
    • :mod:.him — HIMLoco (OpenHomie's HIMPPO): a self-supervised history estimator feeding the actor, plus rollout-time symmetry and mirror losses.
    • :mod:.amp_ppo — PPO plus an adversarial-motion-prior style reward (HUSKY).
    • :mod:.rma — the RMA teacher (actor with estimator + scan / privileged / history encoders, PPO with privileged-latent regularization and DAgger) and its depth-student distillation runner (extreme parkour).

    Each subpackage ships an options class subclassing the rsl_rl option it replaces (RslRlModelOptions / RslRlPpoAlgorithmOptions / RslRlBaseRunnerOptions) whose class_name defaults to its implementation, so a task selects it with actor=<Options>(...), algorithm=<Options>(...) or runner_options=<Options>(...).

    def __init__(
    self,
    obs: TensorDict,
    obs_groups: dict[str, list[str]],
    obs_set: str,
    output_dim: int,
    hidden_dim: int = 512,
    num_blocks: int = 2,
    expansion: int = 4,
    latent_dim: int = 128,
    encoder_hidden_dims: dict[str, list[int]] | None = None,
    default_encoder_hidden_dims: list[int] | tuple[int, ...] = (256,),
    c_shift: float = 3.0,
    compile: bool = False,
    hidden_dims: list[int] | tuple[int, ...] = (),
    activation: str = "swish",
    obs_normalization: bool = True,
    distribution_cfg: dict | None = None,
) -> None:
    if len(hidden_dims) != 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SimBaModel got hidden_dims={list(hidden_dims)}, but SimBa has no plain MLP trunk to size. Set the "
            "backbone with hidden_dim / num_blocks / expansion and the per-group encoders with "
            "encoder_hidden_dims, and leave hidden_dims empty."
        )
    encoder_hidden_dims = dict(encoder_hidden_dims or {})
    unknown = sorted(set(encoder_hidden_dims) - set(obs.keys()))
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SimBaModel encoder_hidden_dims names observation groups {unknown} that the env does not provide; "
            f"available groups: {sorted(obs.keys())}."
        )
    # rsl_rl's MLPModel builds the normaliser, the distribution and a plain MLP trunk; the trunk is replaced
    # below, so build it as small as possible (a 1-wide hidden layer; rsl_rl's MLP needs at least one) rather
    # than at the MLPModel default size.
    super().__init__(
        obs,
        obs_groups,
        obs_set,
        output_dim,
        hidden_dims=[1],
        activation=activation,
        obs_normalization=obs_normalization,
        distribution_cfg=distribution_cfg,
    )
    trunk_output_dim = self.distribution.input_dim if self.distribution is not None else output_dim
    group_dims = [obs[group].shape[-1] for group in self.obs_groups]
    specs = [list(encoder_hidden_dims.get(group, default_encoder_hidden_dims)) for group in self.obs_groups]
    encoder = GroupEncoder(group_dims, specs, latent_dim, resolve_nn_activation(activation))
    self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
        encoder, SimBa(encoder.out_features, trunk_output_dim, hidden_dim, num_blocks, expansion, c_shift)
    )
    if self.distribution is not None:
        self.distribution.init_mlp_weights(self.mlp)
    self._compile_trunk = compile
    self._compiled_trunk = None

    def forward(
    self,
    obs: TensorDict,
    masks: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    hidden_state: Any = None,
    stochastic_output: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    if not self._compile_trunk:
        return super().forward(obs, masks, hidden_state, stochastic_output)
    if self._compiled_trunk is None:
        self._compiled_trunk = torch.compile(
            self.mlp.forward, backend="inductor", mode="default", fullgraph=True, dynamic=False
        )
    obs = unpad_trajectories(obs, masks) if masks is not None and not self.is_recurrent else obs
    latent = self.get_latent(obs, masks, hidden_state)
    trunk_output = self._compiled_trunk(latent)
    if self.distribution is not None:
        if stochastic_output:
            self.distribution.update(trunk_output)
            return self.distribution.sample()
        return self.distribution.deterministic_output(trunk_output)
    return trunk_output

    def update(self) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Run the stock PPO update, and log the value function's explained variance (Weave's extra metric).

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, float]
        rsl_rl's loss dict plus ``explained_variance``.
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        values = self.storage.values.flatten()
        returns = self.storage.returns.flatten()
        explained_variance = (1.0 - (returns - values).var() / (returns.var() + 1e-8)).item()
    loss_dict = super().update()
    loss_dict["explained_variance"] = explained_variance
    return loss_dict

    RslRlAmpPpoAlgorithmOptions ¶

    RslRlAmpPpoAlgorithmOptions(**data)

    Bases: RslRlPpoAlgorithmOptions

    PPO plus an adversarial motion prior (AMP) style reward; defaults are the HUSKY release's.

    The env must publish the observation group amp_obs_group as [joint positions x amp_num_frames (oldest first), style gate]: the style reward is added only where the gate is set (> 0.5), and every window is banked as a policy sample for the discriminator.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    class_name

    The algorithm class rsl_rl resolves; leave at the default.

    TYPE: str

    amp_obs_group

    Observation group carrying the window and the gate.

    TYPE: str

    amp_num_frames

    Frames per window; must equal the group's joint-position history_length.

    def __init__(
    self,
    actor,
    critic,
    storage,
    *,
    amp_motion_file: str,
    amp_obs_group: str = "amp",
    amp_num_frames: int = 5,
    amp_reward_coef: float = 5.0,
    amp_reward_scale: float = 0.02,
    amp_replay_size: int = 100_000,
    amp_discr_hidden_dims: tuple[int, ...] = (256, 256),
    amp_grad_pen_scale: float = 5.0,
    amp_trunk_weight_decay: float = 1e-3,
    amp_head_weight_decay: float = 1e-1,
    amp_warm_start: bool = False,
    **ppo_kwargs,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(actor, critic, storage, **ppo_kwargs)
    self.amp_obs_group = amp_obs_group
    self.amp_warm_start = amp_warm_start
    self.amp_num_frames = amp_num_frames
    self.amp_reward_coef = amp_reward_coef
    self.amp_reward_scale = amp_reward_scale
    self.amp_grad_pen_scale = amp_grad_pen_scale

    self.amp_expert = AmpMotionSampler(amp_motion_file, amp_num_frames, self.device)
    window_dim = self.amp_expert.frame_dim * amp_num_frames
    self.discriminator = AmpDiscriminator(window_dim, tuple(amp_discr_hidden_dims)).to(self.device)
    self.amp_normalizer = FrameNormalizer(self.amp_expert.frame_dim).to(self.device)
    self.amp_replay = AmpReplayBuffer(window_dim, amp_replay_size, self.device)
    self.amp_optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(
        [
            {"params": self.discriminator.trunk.parameters(), "weight_decay": amp_trunk_weight_decay},
            {"params": self.discriminator.head.parameters(), "weight_decay": amp_head_weight_decay},
        ],
        lr=self.learning_rate,
    )
    self._window_dim = window_dim
    # Accumulated as a tensor to avoid a GPU sync inside the rollout loop.
    self._style_reward_sum = torch.zeros((), device=self.device)
    self._style_reward_steps = 0

    @staticmethod
def construct_algorithm(obs: TensorDict, env, cfg: dict, device: str) -> AmpPPO:
    """rsl_rl's PPO construction, then the AMP group checked against the env's first observation."""
    alg = PPO.construct_algorithm(obs, env, cfg, device)
    if alg.amp_obs_group not in obs.keys():
        raise ValueError(
            f"AmpPPO reads the observation group amp_obs_group={alg.amp_obs_group!r}, which the env does not "
            f"provide (groups: {sorted(obs.keys())}). Add it to the task's observation_options, or point "
            "amp_obs_group at the group that carries the AMP window and gate."
        )
    alg._split_amp_obs(obs)  # raises, naming the expected layout, on a mis-sized group
    return alg

    def process_env_step(
    self, obs: TensorDict, rewards: torch.Tensor, dones: torch.Tensor, extras: dict[str, torch.Tensor]
) -> None:
    """Add the gated style reward and bank the policy window, then defer to PPO."""
    raw_windows, gate = self._split_amp_obs(obs)
    frames = raw_windows.view(-1, self.amp_num_frames, self.amp_expert.frame_dim)
    style = self.discriminator.style_reward(self.amp_normalizer.normalize(frames).flatten(1), self.amp_reward_coef)
    style = style * gate.float() * self.amp_reward_scale
    rewards = rewards + style

    self.amp_replay.insert(raw_windows)
    self._style_reward_sum = self._style_reward_sum + style.mean()
    self._style_reward_steps += 1
    super().process_env_step(obs, rewards, dones, extras)

    def update(self) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Run the PPO update, then the discriminator's LSGAN updates."""
    batch_size = self.storage.num_envs * self.storage.num_transitions_per_env // self.num_mini_batches
    loss_dict = super().update()

    # The source trained the discriminator inside the PPO optimizer, so its
    # learning rate followed the KL-adaptive schedule; mirror that here.
    for group in self.amp_optimizer.param_groups:
        group["lr"] = self.learning_rate

    num_updates = self.num_learning_epochs * self.num_mini_batches
    mean_amp_loss = mean_grad_pen = mean_expert_d = mean_policy_d = 0.0
    for _ in range(num_updates):
        policy_windows = self.amp_replay.sample(batch_size).view(-1, self.amp_num_frames, self.amp_expert.frame_dim)
        expert_windows = self.amp_expert.sample(batch_size)
        self.amp_normalizer.update(self._gather(policy_windows[:, -1]))
        self.amp_normalizer.update(self._gather(expert_windows[:, -1]))
        policy_in = self.amp_normalizer.normalize(policy_windows).flatten(1)
        expert_in = self.amp_normalizer.normalize(expert_windows).flatten(1)

        policy_d = self.discriminator(policy_in)
        expert_d = self.discriminator(expert_in)
        expert_loss = torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(expert_d, torch.ones_like(expert_d))
        policy_loss = torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(policy_d, -torch.ones_like(policy_d))
        amp_loss = 0.5 * (expert_loss + policy_loss)
        grad_pen = self.discriminator.gradient_penalty(expert_in, self.amp_grad_pen_scale)

        self.amp_optimizer.zero_grad()
        (amp_loss + grad_pen).backward()
        if self.is_multi_gpu:
            reduce_gradients_in_buckets(
                self.discriminator.parameters(), self.gpu_world_size, self.grad_reduce_bucket_mb
            )
        self.amp_optimizer.step()

        mean_amp_loss += amp_loss.item()
        mean_grad_pen += grad_pen.item()
        mean_expert_d += expert_d.mean().item()
        mean_policy_d += policy_d.mean().item()

    loss_dict["amp"] = mean_amp_loss / num_updates
    loss_dict["amp_grad_pen"] = mean_grad_pen / num_updates
    loss_dict["amp_expert_d"] = mean_expert_d / num_updates
    loss_dict["amp_policy_d"] = mean_policy_d / num_updates
    loss_dict["amp_style_reward"] = float(self._style_reward_sum) / max(self._style_reward_steps, 1)
    self._style_reward_sum = torch.zeros((), device=self.device)
    self._style_reward_steps = 0
    return loss_dict

    def load(self, loaded_dict: dict, load_cfg: dict | None, strict: bool) -> bool:
    """PPO's load, plus the discriminator, its optimizer and the frame normalizer.

    A checkpoint without them was trained as plain PPO. Continuing it under AMP changes the reward under a value
    function trained without the style term, so it is refused unless ``amp_warm_start`` says that is the intent
    (the discriminator then starts fresh).
    """
    missing = [key for key in _AMP_CHECKPOINT_KEYS if key not in loaded_dict]
    if missing and not self.amp_warm_start:
        raise ValueError(
            f"This checkpoint has no AMP state (missing {missing}; it has {sorted(loaded_dict)}), so it was "
            "trained as plain PPO. Loading it into AmpPPO would add the style reward to a value function trained "
            "without it. To start AMP from its weights with a fresh discriminator, set amp_warm_start=True "
            "(--override 'runner_options: {algorithm: {amp_warm_start: true}}'); to replay it, use "
            "`eden inference`, which loads it under stock PPO."
        )
    resumed = super().load(loaded_dict, load_cfg, strict)
    if not missing:
        self.discriminator.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["amp_discriminator_state_dict"], strict=strict)
        if load_cfg is None or load_cfg.get("optimizer"):
            self.amp_optimizer.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["amp_optimizer_state_dict"])
        self.amp_normalizer.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["amp_normalizer_state_dict"])
    return resumed

    Adversarial-motion-prior components used by :class:~eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl.amp_ppo.ppo.AmpPPO.

    Ports the adversarial-motion-prior machinery of TeleHuman/humanoid_skateboarding (its vendored rsl_rl fork: DiscriminatorMulti, G1_AMPLoader, ReplayBufferMulti, Normalizer):

    • :class:AmpMotionSampler draws windows of num_frames consecutive frames (linear interpolation between recorded frames) from expert motion clips. A frame is one joint-position vector, in the order the env's AMP observation group emits it (HUSKY: the G1's 23 no-wrist joints in MJCF order).
    • :class:AmpDiscriminator is the LSGAN discriminator (spectral-norm MLP, expert target +1, policy target -1); its raw output d maps to the style reward coef * clamp(1 - 0.25 (d - 1)^2, min=0).
    • :class:AmpReplayBuffer is a flat ring buffer of policy windows.
    • :class:FrameNormalizer is a running mean/std over single frames, applied per-frame to whole windows before the discriminator.

    Deviation from the source: the source updated its normalizer with already-normalized batches (a bug that decays the statistics toward identity); this one updates from raw frames.

    def __init__(self, motion_file: str, num_frames: int, device: torch.device | str) -> None:
    data = np.load(get_asset_path(motion_file))
    self.device = device
    self.num_frames = num_frames
    self.dt = 1.0 / float(data["fps"])
    self.motions = [
        torch.as_tensor(data[f"motion_{i}"], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
        for i in range(int(data["num_motions"]))
    ]
    self.frame_dim = int(self.motions[0].shape[1])
    for i, motion in enumerate(self.motions):
        if motion.shape[0] < num_frames + 2:
            raise ValueError(f"motion_{i} in {motion_file} is too short ({motion.shape[0]} frames)")

    def sample(self, batch_size: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return expert windows, shape (batch_size, num_frames, frame_dim), oldest frame first."""
    counts = torch.multinomial(
        torch.ones(len(self.motions), device=self.device), batch_size, replacement=True
    ).bincount(minlength=len(self.motions))
    windows = []
    offsets = torch.arange(-(self.num_frames - 2), 2, device=self.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    for motion, count in zip(self.motions, counts.tolist()):
        if count == 0:
            continue
        num_rows = motion.shape[0]
        # Continuous frame index such that every offset stays in [0, num_rows - 1].
        base = torch.empty(count, device=self.device).uniform_(self.num_frames - 2, num_rows - 2)
        idx = base.unsqueeze(1) + offsets.unsqueeze(0)  # (count, num_frames)
        low = idx.floor().long()
        frac = (idx - low.float()).unsqueeze(-1)
        frames = motion[low] * (1.0 - frac) + motion[low + 1] * frac
        windows.append(frames)
    return torch.cat(windows, dim=0)

    def insert(self, windows: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """Insert a batch of flattened windows, overwriting the oldest entries."""
    n = windows.shape[0]
    idx = (self._next + torch.arange(n, device=windows.device)) % self._capacity
    self._buffer[idx] = windows.detach().clone()
    self._next = int((self._next + n) % self._capacity)
    self._size = min(self._size + n, self._capacity)

    def sample(self, batch_size: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    if self._size == 0:
        raise ValueError("AmpReplayBuffer is empty — insert policy windows before sampling.")
    idx = torch.randint(self._size, (batch_size,), device=self._buffer.device)
    return self._buffer[idx]

    @torch.no_grad()
def update(self, frames: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """Fold a batch of raw frames (..., frame_dim) into the running statistics."""
    flat = frames.reshape(-1, frames.shape[-1])
    batch_count = flat.shape[0]
    if batch_count == 0:
        return
    batch_mean = flat.mean(dim=0)
    batch_var = flat.var(dim=0, unbiased=False)
    delta = batch_mean - self.mean
    total = self.count + batch_count
    self.mean += delta * batch_count / total
    m_a = self.var * self.count
    m_b = batch_var * batch_count
    self.var.copy_((m_a + m_b + delta.square() * self.count * batch_count / total) / total)
    self.count.copy_(total)

    def normalize(self, frames: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Normalize frames or windows of frames (..., frame_dim)."""
    std = (self.var + self.eps**2).sqrt()
    return ((frames - self.mean) / std).clamp(-self.clip, self.clip)

    def __init__(self, window_dim: int, hidden_dims: tuple[int, ...] = (256, 256)) -> None:
    super().__init__()
    layers: list[nn.Module] = []
    in_dim = window_dim
    for hidden in hidden_dims:
        layers += [spectral_norm(nn.Linear(in_dim, hidden)), nn.ReLU()]
        in_dim = hidden
    self.trunk = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    self.head = spectral_norm(nn.Linear(in_dim, 1))

    def style_reward(self, windows: torch.Tensor, coef: float) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Per-window style reward ``coef * clamp(1 - 0.25 (d - 1)^2, min=0)``, shape (N,)."""
    with torch.no_grad():
        d = self.forward(windows).squeeze(-1)
    return coef * torch.clamp(1.0 - 0.25 * torch.square(d - 1.0), min=0.0)

    def gradient_penalty(self, expert_windows: torch.Tensor, scale: float) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Penalize the discriminator's gradient norm at the expert samples."""
    expert = expert_windows.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
    d = self.head(self.trunk(expert))
    grad = torch.autograd.grad(
        outputs=d, inputs=expert, grad_outputs=torch.ones_like(d), create_graph=True, retain_graph=True
    )[0]
    return scale * grad.norm(2, dim=1).square().mean()

    def __init__(self, **data):
    # Seed type metadata as construction data so BaseModel validates it into
    # __pydantic_extra__ (no-op for extra="forbid" classes, which use
    # the serialization envelope instead).
    data.update(option_metadata(self))
    # NOTE: all of the option modifications/validations should be done in the __init__ method
    try:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, **data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # A misspelled field on an extra="forbid" class should teach the field set, not just
        # name the typo. Only rewritten when every error is extra_forbidden.
        enriched = _enrich_extra_forbidden(type(self), exc)
        if enriched is None:
            raise
        raise enriched from None

    Bases: MLPModel

    RMA actor over one flat [prop | scan | priv_explicit | priv_latent | history] observation.

    Subclasses rsl_rl's MLPModel for its distribution plumbing (output_*, log-prob, KL, entropy) and its recurrent no-ops, but replaces the trunk: there is no self.mlp, and observation normalization is refused — the task's terms carry hand-tuned fixed scales, and the chunks are sliced by position.

    def __init__(
    self,
    obs: TensorDict,
    obs_groups: dict[str, list[str]],
    obs_set: str,
    output_dim: int,
    num_prop: int = 53,
    num_scan: int = 132,
    num_priv_explicit: int = 9,
    num_priv_latent: int = 29,
    num_hist: int = 10,
    scan_encoder_dims: tuple[int, ...] | list[int] = (128, 64, 32),
    priv_encoder_dims: tuple[int, ...] | list[int] = (64, 20),
    hidden_dims: tuple[int, ...] | list[int] = (512, 256, 128),
    activation: str = "elu",
    estimator_hidden_dims: tuple[int, ...] | list[int] = (128, 64),
    tanh_backbone_output: bool = False,
    obs_normalization: bool = False,
    distribution_cfg: dict | None = None,
) -> None:
    nn.Module.__init__(self)  # not MLPModel.__init__: it would build the plain MLP trunk this model replaces
    if obs_normalization:
        raise ValueError(
            "RmaActorModel(obs_normalization=True): the RMA actor slices its observation by position and trains "
            "on the task's fixed term scales; set obs_normalization=False on the actor options."
        )
    if distribution_cfg is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "RmaActorModel needs a distribution_cfg (the RMA teacher's actor is stochastic); pass "
            "RslRlGaussianDistributionOptions(init_std=1.0, std_type='scalar')."
        )
    self.obs_groups, self.obs_dim = self._get_obs_dim(obs, obs_groups, obs_set)
    self.dims = RmaObsDims(num_prop, num_scan, num_priv_explicit, num_priv_latent, num_hist)
    if self.obs_dim != self.dims.total:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The '{obs_set}' observation set {self.obs_groups} is {self.obs_dim}-d, but the RMA actor options "
            f"describe {self.dims.layout()}. Make the task's {obs_set} groups emit that layout, or set the "
            "actor options' num_prop / num_scan / num_priv_explicit / num_priv_latent / num_hist to the task's."
        )
    self.obs_normalization = False
    self.obs_normalizer = nn.Identity()

    dist_class, dist_cfg = resolve_class(distribution_cfg)
    self.distribution = dist_class(output_dim, **dist_cfg)
    if self.distribution.input_dim != output_dim:
        raise ValueError(
            f"RmaActorModel's backbone emits the {output_dim}-d action mean only; {dist_class.__name__} needs "
            f"{self.distribution.input_dim} inputs. Use a state-independent Gaussian distribution."
        )
    act = resolve_nn_activation(activation)
    self.net = RmaActor(
        self.dims,
        output_dim,
        list(scan_encoder_dims),
        list(priv_encoder_dims),
        list(hidden_dims),
        act,
        tanh_backbone_output=tanh_backbone_output,
    )
    self.estimator = Estimator(num_prop, num_priv_explicit, list(estimator_hidden_dims), act)

    def forward(
    self,
    obs: TensorDict,
    masks: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    hidden_state=None,
    stochastic_output: bool = False,
    *,
    hist_encoding: bool = True,
    estimate: bool = True,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Action (mean, or a sample with ``stochastic_output``); the switches are described in the module docstring."""
    mean = self.mean(self.get_flat_obs(obs), hist_encoding=hist_encoding, estimate=estimate)
    if stochastic_output:
        self.distribution.update(mean)
        return self.distribution.sample()
    return self.distribution.deterministic_output(mean)

    def mean(self, flat: torch.Tensor, *, hist_encoding: bool, estimate: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Action mean from the flat observation (no distribution update)."""
    if estimate:
        flat = self.with_estimate(flat)
    return self.net(flat, hist_encoding)

    def with_estimate(self, flat: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """A copy of ``flat`` whose privileged-explicit chunk is the estimator's prediction (detached).

    Detached: the policy loss never trains the estimator — it has its own regression loss and optimizer.
    """
    d = self.dims
    flat = flat.clone()
    flat[:, d.priv_explicit_slice] = self.estimator(flat[:, d.prop_slice]).detach()
    return flat

    def get_flat_obs(self, obs: TensorDict) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The concatenated observation groups of this model's set."""
    return torch.cat([obs[group] for group in self.obs_groups], dim=-1)

    def __init__(
    self,
    actor: RmaActorModel,
    critic,
    storage,
    *,
    estimator_learning_rate: float = 1.0e-4,
    train_with_estimated_states: bool = True,
    dagger_update_freq: int = 20,
    priv_reg_coef_schedule: tuple[float, float, int, int] | list = (0.0, 0.1, 2000, 3000),
    symmetry_coef: float = 0.0,
    mirror_class_name: str | None = None,
    optimizer: str = "adam",
    **ppo_kwargs,
) -> None:
    if not isinstance(actor, RmaActorModel):
        raise TypeError(
            f"RmaPPO trains an RmaActorModel, got {type(actor).__name__}; set the runner's actor to "
            "RslRlRmaActorOptions(...) (eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl.rma)."
        )
    for key in ("rnd_cfg", "symmetry_cfg", "multi_gpu_cfg"):
        if ppo_kwargs.get(key) is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"RmaPPO does not support {key} (got {ppo_kwargs[key]!r}): leave it None. Its mirror loss is "
                "symmetry_coef + mirror_class_name, and it trains on one GPU — launch without torchrun."
            )
    if ppo_kwargs.get("use_mixed_precision"):
        raise ValueError("RmaPPO does not support use_mixed_precision=True; leave it False.")
    if critic.is_recurrent:
        raise ValueError(
            f"RmaPPO needs a feed-forward critic, got the recurrent {type(critic).__name__}: its update draws flat "
            "mini-batches without hidden states. Use RslRlCriticOptions (an MLP) for the critic."
        )
    if dagger_update_freq < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"RmaPPO(dagger_update_freq={dagger_update_freq}) must be >= 1.")
    if symmetry_coef > 0.0 and mirror_class_name is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"RmaPPO(symmetry_coef={symmetry_coef}) needs mirror_class_name='module.path:Class' — a class built "
            "as Class(dims, device) with mirror_obs(flat) / mirror_action(actions) for the task's layout "
            "(e.g. 'eden.tasks.extreme_parkour.symmetry:ParkourMirror'); or set symmetry_coef=0.0."
        )
    super().__init__(actor, critic, storage, optimizer=optimizer, **ppo_kwargs)
    # PPO's optimizer without the estimator, which trains on its own regression loss (and optimizer) below.
    self.optimizer = resolve_optimizer(optimizer)(
        chain(self.actor.policy_parameters(), self.critic.parameters()), lr=self.learning_rate
    )
    self.estimator_optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.actor.estimator.parameters(), lr=estimator_learning_rate)
    self.hist_encoder_optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(
        self.actor.net.history_encoder.parameters(), lr=self.learning_rate
    )
    self.train_with_estimated_states = train_with_estimated_states
    self.dagger_update_freq = dagger_update_freq
    self.priv_reg_coef_schedule = tuple(priv_reg_coef_schedule)
    self.symmetry_coef = symmetry_coef
    self.mirror = resolve_callable(mirror_class_name)(self.actor.dims, self.device) if symmetry_coef > 0.0 else None
    # Drives the priv-reg ramp; advances on every PPO update and every DAgger update.
    self.counter = 0
    # The learning iteration whose rollout is being collected (the runner's `it`); picks DAgger iterations.
    self.iteration = 0

    def act(self, obs: TensorDict) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sample actions — through the estimator and, on DAgger iterations, the history latent — and record them."""
    self.transition.hidden_states = (self.actor.get_hidden_state(), self.critic.get_hidden_state())
    self.transition.actions = self.actor(
        obs,
        stochastic_output=True,
        hist_encoding=self.is_dagger_iteration,
        estimate=self.train_with_estimated_states,
    ).detach()
    self.transition.values = self.critic(obs).detach()
    self.transition.actions_log_prob = self.actor.get_output_log_prob(self.transition.actions).detach()
    self.transition.distribution_params = tuple(p.detach() for p in self.actor.output_distribution_params)
    self.transition.observations = obs  # ground truth: the estimator's target, the critic's input
    return self.transition.actions

    def update(self) -> dict[str, float]:
    """PPO epochs with the estimator, priv-reg and mirror terms; then DAgger on DAgger iterations."""
    actor, dims = self.actor, self.actor.dims
    mean_value_loss = mean_surrogate_loss = mean_entropy = 0.0
    mean_priv_reg_loss = mean_estimator_loss = mean_symmetry_loss = 0.0
    priv_reg_coef = 0.0
    start, end, ramp_start, ramp_len = self.priv_reg_coef_schedule

    for batch in self.storage.mini_batch_generator(self.num_mini_batches, self.num_learning_epochs):
        if self.normalize_advantage_per_mini_batch:  # else compute_returns normalized them over the rollout
            with torch.no_grad():
                batch.advantages = (batch.advantages - batch.advantages.mean()) / (batch.advantages.std() + 1e-8)
        # PPO always trains through the privileged path on the stored ground truth; the history encoder trains
        # in the DAgger update only.
        actor(batch.observations, stochastic_output=True, hist_encoding=False, estimate=False)
        actions_log_prob = actor.get_output_log_prob(batch.actions)
        values = self.critic(batch.observations)
        distribution_params = actor.output_distribution_params
        mu = actor.output_mean
        entropy = actor.output_entropy
        flat = actor.get_flat_obs(batch.observations)

        # Privileged regularization toward the frozen history latent, coefficient ramped by the counter.
        priv_latent = actor.net.infer_priv_latent(flat)
        with torch.no_grad():
            hist_latent = actor.net.infer_hist_latent(flat)
        priv_reg_loss = (priv_latent - hist_latent).norm(p=2, dim=1).mean()
        priv_reg_coef = start + min(max(self.counter - ramp_start, 0) / ramp_len, 1.0) * (end - start)

        # Estimator step on its own optimizer: the stored obs carry the ground-truth priv_explicit.
        predicted = actor.estimator(flat[:, dims.prop_slice])
        estimator_loss = (predicted - flat[:, dims.priv_explicit_slice]).pow(2).mean()
        self.estimator_optimizer.zero_grad()
        estimator_loss.backward()
        nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(actor.estimator.parameters(), self.max_grad_norm)
        self.estimator_optimizer.step()

        if self.desired_kl is not None and self.schedule == "adaptive":
            with torch.inference_mode():
                kl_mean = actor.get_kl_divergence(batch.old_distribution_params, distribution_params).mean()
                if kl_mean > self.desired_kl * 2.0:
                    self.learning_rate = max(1e-5, self.learning_rate / 1.5)
                elif kl_mean < self.desired_kl / 2.0 and kl_mean > 0.0:
                    self.learning_rate = min(1e-2, self.learning_rate * 1.5)
                for param_group in self.optimizer.param_groups:
                    param_group["lr"] = self.learning_rate

        ratio = torch.exp(actions_log_prob - torch.squeeze(batch.old_actions_log_prob))
        surrogate = -torch.squeeze(batch.advantages) * ratio
        surrogate_clipped = -torch.squeeze(batch.advantages) * torch.clamp(
            ratio, 1.0 - self.clip_param, 1.0 + self.clip_param
        )
        surrogate_loss = torch.max(surrogate, surrogate_clipped).mean()

        if self.use_clipped_value_loss:
            value_clipped = batch.values + (values - batch.values).clamp(-self.clip_param, self.clip_param)
            value_loss = torch.max((values - batch.returns).pow(2), (value_clipped - batch.returns).pow(2)).mean()
        else:
            value_loss = (batch.returns - values).pow(2).mean()

        # Mirror equivariance on the action mean; both sides carry gradient.
        symmetry_loss = torch.zeros((), device=self.device)
        if self.mirror is not None:
            mu_mirrored = actor.mean(self.mirror.mirror_obs(flat), hist_encoding=False, estimate=False)
            symmetry_loss = (mu_mirrored - self.mirror.mirror_action(mu)).pow(2).mean()

        loss = (
            surrogate_loss
            + self.value_loss_coef * value_loss
            - self.entropy_coef * entropy.mean()
            + priv_reg_coef * priv_reg_loss
            + self.symmetry_coef * symmetry_loss
        )
        self.optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(chain(actor.policy_parameters(), self.critic.parameters()), self.max_grad_norm)
        self.optimizer.step()

        mean_value_loss += value_loss.item()
        mean_surrogate_loss += surrogate_loss.item()
        mean_entropy += entropy.mean().item()
        mean_priv_reg_loss += priv_reg_loss.item()
        mean_estimator_loss += estimator_loss.item()
        mean_symmetry_loss += symmetry_loss.item()

    self.critic.update_normalization(self.storage.observations.flatten(0, 1))
    self.counter += 1
    num_updates = self.num_learning_epochs * self.num_mini_batches
    loss_dict = {
        "value": mean_value_loss / num_updates,
        "surrogate": mean_surrogate_loss / num_updates,
        "entropy": mean_entropy / num_updates,
        "priv_reg": mean_priv_reg_loss / num_updates,
        "priv_reg_coef": priv_reg_coef,
        "estimator": mean_estimator_loss / num_updates,
    }
    if self.mirror is not None:
        loss_dict["symmetry"] = mean_symmetry_loss / num_updates
    if self.is_dagger_iteration:
        loss_dict["hist_latent"] = self.update_dagger()
    self.storage.clear()
    self.iteration += 1
    return loss_dict

    def update_dagger(self) -> float:
    """Regress the history (adaptation) encoder onto the privileged latent over the stored rollout."""
    actor = self.actor
    mean_loss = 0.0
    for batch in self.storage.mini_batch_generator(self.num_mini_batches, self.num_learning_epochs):
        flat = actor.get_flat_obs(batch.observations)
        with torch.no_grad():
            priv_latent = actor.net.infer_priv_latent(flat)
        hist_latent_loss = (priv_latent - actor.net.infer_hist_latent(flat)).norm(p=2, dim=1).mean()
        self.hist_encoder_optimizer.zero_grad()
        hist_latent_loss.backward()
        nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(actor.net.history_encoder.parameters(), self.max_grad_norm)
        self.hist_encoder_optimizer.step()
        mean_loss += hist_latent_loss.item()
    self.counter += 1
    return mean_loss / (self.num_learning_epochs * self.num_mini_batches)

    def load(self, loaded_dict: dict, load_cfg: dict | None, strict: bool) -> bool:
    """PPO's load — with the actor checked key for key whatever ``strict`` says — plus the RMA state.

    Eden loads with ``strict=False`` to tolerate drift, but a partially loaded RMA actor (another model's
    checkpoint, e.g. a plain MLP actor's ``mlp.*``) would run with random encoders or estimator.
    """
    if (load_cfg is None or load_cfg.get("actor")) and "actor_state_dict" in loaded_dict:
        expected, found = set(self._raw_actor.state_dict()), set(loaded_dict["actor_state_dict"])
        if expected != found:
            raise ValueError(
                "This checkpoint's actor_state_dict is not an RmaActorModel's: missing "
                f"{sorted(expected - found)[:6]}{' ...' if len(expected - found) > 6 else ''}, unexpected "
                f"{sorted(found - expected)[:6]}{' ...' if len(found - expected) > 6 else ''}. It was saved by "
                "another actor model (or an RMA actor with other layers); load it with the task that trained it."
            )
    load_iteration = super().load(loaded_dict, load_cfg, strict)
    if load_cfg is None or load_cfg.get("optimizer"):
        for key, opt in (
            ("estimator_optimizer_state_dict", self.estimator_optimizer),
            ("hist_encoder_optimizer_state_dict", self.hist_encoder_optimizer),
        ):
            if key in loaded_dict:  # absent from a checkpoint another algorithm saved: keep the fresh state
                opt.load_state_dict(loaded_dict[key])
    if load_iteration:
        # The runner resumes at the saved iteration number, so the DAgger cadence and the ramp continue.
        self.iteration = loaded_dict["iter"]
        self.counter = loaded_dict.get("rma_counter", self.counter)
    return load_iteration

    DAgger depth distillation of an RMA teacher into a depth-camera student (rsl-rl-lib >= 5.5.1).

    Port of the vision distillation loop from "Extreme Parkour with Legged Robots" (Cheng et al. 2023). The frozen teacher (:class:~eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl.rma.model.RmaActorModel, history-latent path, true scandots, ground truth privileged-explicit chunk) labels every step; the student — depth_actor (a copy of the teacher's actor net) fed by a recurrent depth_encoder whose latent replaces the scan latent — acts and drives the environment from its depth latent and its own prediction of the delta-yaw slots; one optimizer step per iteration regresses student -> teacher actions plus the yaw prediction, backpropagating through the whole iteration's graph.

    That loop fits neither rsl_rl's Distillation (which stores observations and trains on mini-batches) nor its runner loop (which collects under torch.inference_mode), so this module ships its own runner, :class:RmaDepthDistillationRunner — what :class:~eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl.rma.options.RslRlRmaDepthDistillationRunnerOptions's class_name names, so eden train --task extreme_parkour_student --checkpoint <teacher model_<it>.pt> runs it.

    Cadence contract: the depth encoder runs only on control steps where the env refreshed the depth observation (common_step_counter % update_interval == 0); between refreshes the cached latent/yaw are reused. Every observation term of the student's groups that declares an update_interval must run at the same cadence (checked against the live env at construction), and num_steps_per_env must be a positive multiple of it so an iteration boundary never splits a cadence window (the update would otherwise backprop into the previous iteration's freed graph).

    Checkpoints carry the teacher (actor_state_dict, estimator included — the same key a teacher checkpoint has) plus depth_actor_state_dict / depth_encoder_state_dict / depth_optimizer_state_dict. load() accepts either: a teacher checkpoint starts a fresh distillation (student actor re-copied from the teacher), a student checkpoint resumes one. Only a student checkpoint (or a student trained in this process) replays: :meth:RmaDepthDistillationRunner.get_inference_policy refuses an untrained depth encoder.

    Like the source, the student reads the privileged-explicit chunk (base linear velocity) as the env provides it — in sim, the ground truth — in distillation and in replay alike. It is an in-sim policy: eden deploy refuses this runner, and a hardware port would have to substitute the frozen teacher's estimator for that chunk (in distillation too, so the student trains on what it would see).

    def __init__(
    self,
    teacher: RmaActorModel,
    *,
    depth_obs_group: str = _STUDENT_GROUP_KEYS["depth_obs_group"],
    yaw_gate_obs_group: str = _STUDENT_GROUP_KEYS["yaw_gate_obs_group"],
    yaw_slots: tuple[int, int] | list[int] = (6, 8),
    update_interval: int = 5,
    num_pretrain_iters: int = 0,
    gru_hidden_dim: int = 512,
    learning_rate: float = 1.0e-3,
    max_grad_norm: float = 1.0,
    yaw_scale: float = 1.5,
    device: str = "cpu",
    multi_gpu_cfg: dict | None = None,
) -> None:
    if multi_gpu_cfg is not None:
        raise ValueError("RmaDepthDistillation is single-GPU; launch without torchrun.")
    start, stop = yaw_slots
    if not (0 <= start < stop <= teacher.dims.num_prop and stop - start == 2):
        raise ValueError(
            f"yaw_slots={tuple(yaw_slots)} must name the 2 (delta_yaw, delta_next_yaw) slots inside the "
            f"{teacher.dims.num_prop}-d proprioception chunk; the yaw head predicts exactly 2 values."
        )
    self.device = device
    self.dims = teacher.dims
    self.depth_obs_group = depth_obs_group
    self.yaw_gate_obs_group = yaw_gate_obs_group
    self.yaw_slice = slice(start, stop)
    self.update_interval = update_interval
    self.num_pretrain_iters = num_pretrain_iters
    self.yaw_scale = yaw_scale
    self.max_grad_norm = max_grad_norm
    self.teacher = teacher.to(device).requires_grad_(False)
    self.teacher_loaded = False
    # Whether the depth encoder / actor hold a trained student (loaded, or updated in this process).
    self.student_ready = False
    # The depth latent substitutes for the teacher's scan latent, so its width is the scan latent's width.
    self.depth_encoder = RecurrentDepthEncoder(
        num_prop=self.dims.num_prop, latent_dim=teacher.net.scan_latent_dim, gru_hidden_dim=gru_hidden_dim
    ).to(device)
    self.depth_actor = copy.deepcopy(self.teacher.net).requires_grad_(True).to(device)
    self.optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(
        [*self.depth_actor.parameters(), *self.depth_encoder.parameters()], lr=learning_rate
    )

    @staticmethod
def construct_algorithm(obs: TensorDict, env, cfg: dict, device: str) -> RmaDepthDistillation:
    """Build the teacher from ``cfg["actor"]`` (it must match the teacher checkpoint) and the student around it."""
    alg_class, alg_cfg = resolve_class(cfg["algorithm"])
    actor_class, actor_cfg = resolve_class(cfg["actor"])
    cfg["obs_groups"] = resolve_obs_groups(obs, cfg["obs_groups"], ["actor"])
    for key, default in _STUDENT_GROUP_KEYS.items():
        group = alg_cfg.get(key, default)
        if group not in obs.keys():
            raise ValueError(
                f"Depth distillation reads the observation group algorithm.{key}={group!r}, which the env does "
                f"not provide (groups: {sorted(obs.keys())}). Is the env the depth-student task?"
            )
    teacher = actor_class(obs, cfg["obs_groups"], "actor", env.num_actions, **actor_cfg)
    if not isinstance(teacher, RmaActorModel):
        raise TypeError(
            "Depth distillation needs an RmaActorModel teacher (actor=RslRlRmaActorOptions(...)), got "
            f"{type(teacher).__name__}."
        )
    return alg_class(teacher, device=device, **alg_cfg, multi_gpu_cfg=cfg["multi_gpu"])

    def encode(self, depth_frame: torch.Tensor, flat: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """One depth-encoder pass: ``(depth latent, scaled 2-d yaw prediction)``.

    The proprioception chunk is fed with the yaw slots hidden (the student must recover heading from depth); the
    Tanh-bounded yaw head is stretched by ``yaw_scale``. Shared by the training loop and the inference policy so
    the encoding contract cannot drift between them.
    """
    prop = flat[:, self.dims.prop_slice].clone()
    prop[:, self.yaw_slice] = 0.0
    latent_and_yaw = self.depth_encoder(depth_frame, prop)
    return latent_and_yaw[:, :-2], self.yaw_scale * latent_and_yaw[:, -2:]

    update ¶
    update(action_diffs: Tensor, yaw_errors: Tensor) -> dict[str, float]

    One optimizer step on the iteration's teacher - student actions and true - predicted yaw errors.

    Both losses are mean per-sample L2 norms; the gradient clip covers the actor only (faithful to the source).

    def update(self, action_diffs: torch.Tensor, yaw_errors: torch.Tensor) -> dict[str, float]:
    """One optimizer step on the iteration's ``teacher - student`` actions and ``true - predicted`` yaw errors.

    Both losses are mean per-sample L2 norms; the gradient clip covers the actor only (faithful to the source).
    """
    action_loss = action_diffs.norm(p=2, dim=1).mean()
    yaw_loss = yaw_errors.norm(p=2, dim=1).mean()
    loss = action_loss + yaw_loss
    self.optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.depth_actor.parameters(), self.max_grad_norm)
    self.optimizer.step()
    self.student_ready = True
    return {"depth_actor": action_loss.item(), "yaw": yaw_loss.item(), "total": loss.item()}

    def load(self, loaded_dict: dict, *, load_optimizer: bool = True) -> bool:
    """Load the teacher, and the student halves when present; ``True`` when it resumed a student."""
    self.teacher.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["actor_state_dict"])
    self.teacher_loaded = True
    if "depth_actor_state_dict" not in loaded_dict:
        self.depth_actor.load_state_dict(self.teacher.net.state_dict())  # a fresh distillation from the teacher
        return False
    self.depth_actor.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["depth_actor_state_dict"])
    self.depth_encoder.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["depth_encoder_state_dict"])
    if load_optimizer:
        self.optimizer.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["depth_optimizer_state_dict"])
    self.student_ready = True
    return True

    def __init__(self, env, train_cfg: dict, log_dir: str | None = None, device: str = "cpu") -> None:
    if eden_dist.is_distributed():
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Depth distillation is single-GPU: it has no parameter broadcast or gradient reduction, so a "
            "distributed launch would train an independent student per rank. Launch without torchrun."
        )
    super().__init__(env, train_cfg, log_dir=log_dir, device=device)
    interval, steps = self.alg.update_interval, self.cfg["num_steps_per_env"]
    if steps <= 0 or steps % interval != 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"num_steps_per_env ({steps}) must be a positive multiple of algorithm.update_interval ({interval}), "
            "so an iteration boundary never splits a depth-refresh window."
        )
    self._validate_env_cadence()

    def learn(self, num_learning_iterations: int, init_at_random_ep_len: bool = False) -> None:
    """The vision DAgger loop; ``init_at_random_ep_len`` spreads the envs' episode clocks, as rsl_rl's loop does."""
    if not self.alg.teacher_loaded:
        raise ValueError(self.checkpoint_required)
    alg, env_unwrapped = self.alg, self.env.unwrapped
    interval = alg.update_interval
    check_for_nan = self.cfg.get("check_for_nan", True)
    if init_at_random_ep_len:
        self.env.episode_length_buf = torch.randint_like(
            self.env.episode_length_buf, high=int(self.env.max_episode_length)
        )
    obs = self.env.get_observations().to(self.device)
    alg.train_mode()
    self.logger.init_logging_writer()
    depth_latent: torch.Tensor | None = None
    yaw_pred: torch.Tensor | None = None

    start_it = self.current_learning_iteration
    total_it = start_it + num_learning_iterations
    for it in range(start_it, total_it):
        start = time.time()
        action_diffs: list[torch.Tensor] = []
        yaw_errors: list[torch.Tensor] = []
        gate_fracs: list[torch.Tensor] = []  # 0-d tensors; one host sync per iteration
        # NO torch.inference_mode (unlike PPO): the student's actions carry the graph the update backpropagates.
        for _ in range(self.cfg["num_steps_per_env"]):
            # Clone: the yaw substitution must not leak into the env-owned observation buffer.
            flat = alg.teacher.get_flat_obs(obs).clone()
            gate = obs[alg.yaw_gate_obs_group].squeeze(-1) > 0.5
            if depth_latent is None or env_unwrapped.common_step_counter % interval == 0:
                depth_latent, yaw_pred = alg.encode(obs[alg.depth_obs_group], flat)
                yaw_errors.append(flat[:, alg.yaw_slice] - yaw_pred)
            # The label comes BEFORE the yaw substitution: the teacher sees the true delta-yaw.
            teacher_actions = alg.teacher_actions(obs)
            gate_fracs.append(gate.float().mean())
            # The student sees its own (detached) yaw prediction wherever the gate allows; the yaw head trains
            # only through the auxiliary loss, as in the source.
            flat[gate, alg.yaw_slice] = yaw_pred.detach()[gate]
            student_actions = alg.student_actions(flat, depth_latent)
            action_diffs.append(teacher_actions - student_actions)

            stepped = teacher_actions if it < alg.num_pretrain_iters else student_actions
            obs, rewards, dones, extras = self.env.step(stepped.detach().to(self.env.device))
            if check_for_nan:
                check_nan(obs, rewards, dones)
            obs, rewards, dones = obs.to(self.device), rewards.to(self.device), dones.to(self.device)
            self.logger.process_env_step(rewards, dones, extras, None)

        stop = time.time()
        collect_time, start = stop - start, stop

        loss_dict = alg.update(torch.cat(action_diffs), torch.cat(yaw_errors))
        loss_dict["delta_yaw_ok_frac"] = torch.stack(gate_fracs).mean().item()
        alg.depth_encoder.detach_hidden()
        # Force a fresh encoder pass at the next iteration's first step: reusing the latent across the update
        # would backprop into the freed graph.
        depth_latent = yaw_pred = None

        learn_time = time.time() - start
        self.current_learning_iteration = it
        self.logger.log(
            it=it,
            start_it=start_it,
            total_it=total_it,
            collect_time=collect_time,
            learn_time=learn_time,
            loss_dict=loss_dict,
            learning_rate=alg.optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"],
            # Distillation is deterministic — no exploration noise to report.
            action_std=torch.zeros(self.env.num_actions, device=self.device),
            rnd_weight=None,
        )
        if self.logger.writer is not None and self._save_due(it, start_it):
            self.save(os.path.join(self.logger.log_dir, f"model_{it}.pt"))

    if self.logger.writer is not None:
        self.save(os.path.join(self.logger.log_dir, f"model_{self.current_learning_iteration}.pt"))
        self.logger.stop_logging_writer()

    def load(self, path: str, load_optimizer: bool = True, map_location: str | None = None) -> dict | None:
    """Load a teacher checkpoint (fresh distillation) or a student checkpoint (resume)."""
    loaded_dict = torch.load(path, weights_only=False, map_location=map_location)
    if "actor_state_dict" not in loaded_dict:
        raise ValueError(
            f"'{path}' has no 'actor_state_dict' (keys: {sorted(loaded_dict)}), so it is not an RMA teacher or "
            "student checkpoint of the rsl-rl-lib 5 layout. An rsl_rl 3 checkpoint ('model_state_dict') does not "
            "load here: retrain the teacher with `eden train --task extreme_parkour_teacher`."
        )
    if self.alg.load(loaded_dict, load_optimizer=load_optimizer):
        self.current_learning_iteration = loaded_dict["iter"]
    return loaded_dict.get("infos")

    def get_inference_policy(self, device: str | None = None) -> Callable[[TensorDict], torch.Tensor]:
    """The deployed student: depth encoder every ``update_interval`` steps, its yaw in the yaw slots.

    The yaw prediction replaces the yaw slots unconditionally (the source's play behavior — the gate is a
    training-time aid), and the privileged-explicit chunk stays as the env provides it (in-sim ground truth; a
    hardware deployment would substitute the teacher's estimator here).
    """
    alg, env_unwrapped = self.alg, self.env.unwrapped
    if not alg.student_ready:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "The depth student has not been trained: this runner loaded a teacher checkpoint (no "
            "depth_actor_state_dict / depth_encoder_state_dict), so its depth encoder is randomly initialized and "
            "would drive the robot from a random latent and a random yaw. Replay a student checkpoint (a model_<it>.pt "
            "written by `eden train --task extreme_parkour_student`), or replay the teacher itself with "
            "--task extreme_parkour_teacher."
        )
    alg.eval_mode()
    if device is not None:
        alg.depth_actor.to(device)
        alg.depth_encoder.to(device)
    alg.depth_encoder.reset_hidden()
    state: dict[str, torch.Tensor | None] = {"latent": None, "yaw": None}

    def act(obs: TensorDict) -> torch.Tensor:
        with torch.no_grad():
            flat = alg.teacher.get_flat_obs(obs).clone()
            if state["latent"] is None or env_unwrapped.common_step_counter % alg.update_interval == 0:
                state["latent"], state["yaw"] = alg.encode(obs[alg.depth_obs_group], flat)
            flat[:, alg.yaw_slice] = state["yaw"]
            return alg.student_actions(flat, state["latent"])

    return act

    HIMPPOAlgorithmOptions ¶

    HIMPPOAlgorithmOptions(**data)

    Bases: RslRlPpoAlgorithmOptions

    PPO options for OpenHomie's HIMLoco learner.

    Built by rsl-rl-lib's own OnPolicyRunner on any major Eden supports (3, 4, 5), so eden train and eden inference need nothing algorithm-specific; :meth:adapt_runner_dict routes the construction for the installed major. The task supplies the two things that tie HIMPPO to an observation layout:

    • the observation groups: obs_groups["actor"] one group of stacked frames, obs_groups["critic"] one group of a single frame + the true base linear velocity (3, last);
    • the mirror, data_augmentation_func.
    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    data_augmentation_func

    "module:function" mirroring the task's observations and actions, with rsl-rl-lib's symmetry signature f(env=, obs=TensorDict | None, actions=Tensor | None) -> (obs_aug, actions_aug), each the input stacked with its mirror along the batch axis — the same function stock PPO's symmetry extension takes. Required: every transition is stored with its mirror.
    use_flip

    Also train the estimator on mirrored observations and add the actor and critic mirror losses (OpenHomie use_flip). Symmetry lives here, so symmetry_cfg must stay None.
    symmetry_scale

    Weight of the two mirror losses.
    target_skip_dim

    Leading entries of the next critic observation the SwAV target encoder leaves out (OpenHomie drops the three velocity commands a frame starts with).

    def __init__(self, **data):
    # Seed type metadata as construction data so BaseModel validates it into
    # __pydantic_extra__ (no-op for extra="forbid" classes, which use
    # the serialization envelope instead).
    data.update(option_metadata(self))
    # NOTE: all of the option modifications/validations should be done in the __init__ method
    try:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, **data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # A misspelled field on an extra="forbid" class should teach the field set, not just
        # name the typo. Only rewritten when every error is extra_forbidden.
        enriched = _enrich_extra_forbidden(type(self), exc)
        if enriched is None:
            raise
        raise enriched from None

    def adapt_runner_dict(self, runner_dict: dict, major: int) -> dict:
    """Point the version-translated runner dict at HIM's constructors for rsl-rl-lib ``major``.

    4 and 5 build the algorithm through ``class_name`` → ``construct_algorithm``, which reads the
    translated dict as it is. 3 builds the model from ``policy.class_name`` and calls the algorithm
    class with it, so both go to HIM's v3 factories, and the model gets ``target_skip_dim``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runner_dict: dict
        The dict :func:`~eden.options.learning.rsl_rl.translate.translate_runner_dict` produced for ``major``.
    major: int
        The installed rsl-rl-lib major version.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``runner_dict``, adapted in place.
    """
    if major == 3:
        module = "eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl.him"
        runner_dict["policy"]["class_name"] = f"{module}.actor_critic:HIMActorCritic.from_rsl_rl_v3"
        runner_dict["policy"]["target_skip_dim"] = self.target_skip_dim
        runner_dict["algorithm"]["class_name"] = f"{module}.ppo:HIMPPO.from_rsl_rl_v3"
    return runner_dict

    def __init__(
    self,
    actor_critic: HIMActorCritic,
    use_flip: bool = True,
    num_learning_epochs: int = 5,
    num_mini_batches: int = 4,
    clip_param: float = 0.2,
    gamma: float = 0.99,
    lam: float = 0.95,
    value_loss_coef: float = 1.0,
    entropy_coef: float = 0.01,
    learning_rate: float = 1e-3,
    max_grad_norm: float = 1.0,
    use_clipped_value_loss: bool = True,
    schedule: str = "adaptive",
    desired_kl: float = 0.01,
    device: str = "cpu",
    symmetry_scale: float = 1.0,
    env=None,
    data_augmentation_func: Callable | None = None,
):
    if data_augmentation_func is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "HIMPPO stores every transition's mirror, so it needs the task's mirror: set the algorithm options' "
            "data_augmentation_func to a 'module:function' with rsl-rl's symmetry signature."
        )
    self.env = env
    self.data_augmentation_func = data_augmentation_func
    self.device = device
    self.use_flip = use_flip
    self.desired_kl = desired_kl
    self.schedule = schedule
    self.learning_rate = learning_rate

    self.actor_critic = actor_critic
    self.actor_critic.to(self.device)
    self.storage: HIMRolloutStorage | None = None
    self.optimizer = HIMOptimizer(
        optim.Adam(self.actor_critic.parameters(), lr=learning_rate), self.actor_critic.estimator.optimizer
    )
    self.transition = HIMRolloutStorage.Transition()
    self.transition_sym = HIMRolloutStorage.Transition()
    self.symmetry_scale = symmetry_scale

    self.clip_param = clip_param
    self.num_learning_epochs = num_learning_epochs
    self.num_mini_batches = num_mini_batches
    self.value_loss_coef = value_loss_coef
    self.entropy_coef = entropy_coef
    self.gamma = gamma
    self.lam = lam
    self.max_grad_norm = max_grad_norm
    self.use_clipped_value_loss = use_clipped_value_loss

    # Read by rsl-rl-lib's runners: RND is logged when an algorithm has it, and v3 reaches the
    # model as ``alg.policy`` (v4/v5 through ``get_policy()``).
    self.rnd = None
    self.intrinsic_rewards = None
    self.policy = actor_critic
    self.actor_obs_group = actor_critic.obs_group
    self.critic_obs_group = actor_critic.critic_obs_group

def construct_algorithm(cls, obs, env, cfg: dict, device: str) -> HIMPPO:
    """rsl-rl-lib 4 / 5's construction hook: build the actor-critic, the storage and the algorithm.

    The mirror is run once on these observations' widths, so a layout it does not cover fails here,
    before a rollout.
    """
    if cfg.get("multi_gpu"):
        raise NotImplementedError(_NOT_DISTRIBUTED)
    cfg["obs_groups"] = resolve_obs_groups(obs, cfg["obs_groups"], ["actor", "critic"])
    actor_cfg, critic_cfg = cfg["actor"], cfg["critic"]
    if actor_cfg.get("obs_normalization") or critic_cfg.get("obs_normalization"):
        raise ValueError(_NO_OBS_NORMALIZATION)
    init_std = check_model_cfg(actor_cfg, critic_cfg)
    # Without the pre-reset critic observations every rollout would fail on its first step; refuse here.
    env_options = getattr(getattr(env, "unwrapped", env), "env_options", None)
    if env_options is not None and not getattr(env_options, "record_final_observations", True):
        raise ValueError(_NEEDS_FINAL_OBSERVATIONS)
    actor_critic = HIMActorCritic.from_groups(
        obs,
        single_group(cfg["obs_groups"], "actor"),
        single_group(cfg["obs_groups"], "critic"),
        env.num_actions,
        actor_hidden_dims=actor_cfg["hidden_dims"],
        critic_hidden_dims=critic_cfg["hidden_dims"],
        activation=actor_cfg["activation"],
        init_noise_std=init_std,
        target_skip_dim=cfg["algorithm"]["target_skip_dim"],
    )
    return cls._build(actor_critic, cfg["algorithm"], device, env, env.num_envs, cfg["num_steps_per_env"])

    @classmethod
def from_rsl_rl_v3(
    cls, actor_critic: HIMActorCritic, storage, device: str, multi_gpu_cfg=None, **alg_cfg
) -> HIMPPO:
    """rsl-rl-lib 3's construction call, ``alg_class(actor_critic, storage, device=, **alg_cfg, multi_gpu_cfg=)``.

    Reached through the ``algorithm.class_name`` that ``HIMPPOAlgorithmOptions.adapt_runner_dict`` writes;
    the runner has already built ``actor_critic`` (``HIMActorCritic.from_rsl_rl_v3``). Its stock rollout
    storage is only read for its size. v3 hands the algorithm no env, so the mirror gets ``env=None``.
    """
    if multi_gpu_cfg:
        raise NotImplementedError(_NOT_DISTRIBUTED)
    return cls._build(actor_critic, alg_cfg, device, None, storage.num_envs, storage.num_transitions_per_env)

    def load(self, loaded_dict: dict, load_cfg: dict | None = None, strict: bool = True) -> bool:
    """Load what ``load_cfg`` selects (everything when ``None``); return whether to restore the iteration.

    The weights always load strictly, whatever ``strict`` says. Eden's checkpoint loader passes
    ``strict=False`` so stock PPO can take older rsl-rl layouts, but a HIM checkpoint has one layout: a
    missing or extra key means the wrong checkpoint, and loading past it would leave those weights at
    their random init. ``ValueError``, not ``KeyError``, so the loader does not reword it as an
    rsl-rl version mismatch.
    """
    if load_cfg is None:
        load_cfg = {"actor": True, "critic": True, "optimizer": True, "iteration": True}
    if "actor_critic_state_dict" not in loaded_dict:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Not a HIMPPO checkpoint from rsl-rl-lib 4/5: no 'actor_critic_state_dict' among "
            f"{sorted(loaded_dict)}. A stock-PPO or rsl-rl-lib 3 checkpoint cannot initialize HIMPPO; "
            f"pass a checkpoint this algorithm saved."
        )
    if load_cfg.get("actor") or load_cfg.get("critic"):
        state = loaded_dict["actor_critic_state_dict"]
        expected = set(self.actor_critic.state_dict())
        missing, unexpected = sorted(expected - set(state)), sorted(set(state) - expected)
        if missing or unexpected:
            raise ValueError(
                f"HIMPPO checkpoint does not match this actor-critic: missing {missing}, unexpected "
                f"{unexpected}. It was saved for a different observation layout or network; train or "
                f"pick a checkpoint from this task's config."
            )
        self.actor_critic.load_state_dict(state, strict=True)
    if load_cfg.get("optimizer"):
        self.optimizer.ppo.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["optimizer_state_dict"])
        self.optimizer.estimator.load_state_dict(loaded_dict["estimator_optimizer_state_dict"])
        self.learning_rate = self.optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"]
    return bool(load_cfg.get("iteration", False))

    def process_env_step(self, obs, rewards, dones, extras) -> None:
    """Record the step; ``obs`` is the observation *after* it, post-reset for the envs that ended.

    The estimator's target is the true next critic observation, so the ended envs take their
    pre-reset one from ``extras["final_observations"]`` — OpenHomie's
    ``next_critic_obs[termination_ids] = termination_privileged_obs``.
    """
    final = extras.get("final_observations")
    if final is None:
        raise KeyError(_NEEDS_FINAL_OBSERVATIONS)
    next_critic_obs = torch.where(
        dones.bool().unsqueeze(-1), final[self.critic_obs_group].to(self.device), obs[self.critic_obs_group]
    )
    self._process_env_step(rewards, dones, extras, next_critic_obs)
